scope: Proposition 4.1 (The minor-arc moment) of the manuscript “The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors” (preprints/The-Poisson-Dirichlet-Law-for-Prime-Predecessors-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 011 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4b54d35506a19280), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed E0 > 0, one can choose A0 sufficiently large and then K sufficiently large, in terms of E0, q and the fixed parameters of Theorem 3.1, so that the operator with the good-state projections satisfies 1 UV X P∈Ω P primitive ⟨uP , (AA∗ )R uP ⟩ ≤ L−E0N . (4.1) The choices of A0, K do not depend on the particular fixed band exponents a1 < · · · < aK; the threshold for x may depend on them. Consequently, for any prescribed fixed A > 0, the determinant indicator in the expanded square of the preceding section can be replaced by (3.11), with error OA(XY L−A). In the resulting major term the disjointness restriction on the two unshared products a, b can be omitted. Equivalently, with the notation of (3.8) and (5.1), |QY − Qmaj Y | ≪A XY L−A . (4.2) The precision needed in the pairing estimate (3.20) for this consequence is independent of K.
